title: Large tools split along their change boundaries without blocking work
goal: kbgit.py and backlog.py keep only their command line, usage text and dispatch, with their code in kg_ and bl_ modules, their tests and fixtures split to match and every test name kept; a task that moves code out of a shared file is announced, waits for no claimed item on the file and lands as one atomic commit; each bl_ module owns its tools.md row and backlog.md section, and each registers its own parsers

gates.question: Approve this sprint's goal and committed items?

notes: Rank 2 of the 5 active sprints. Ends the split of the two largest tools: backlog.py and kbgit.py keep only their command line, usage and dispatch, with the code in bl_ and kg_ modules and every test name kept. The kbgit.py split is complete; ST-pkprc4oy “kbgit.py splits along its change boundaries behind the unchanged CLI” and ST-e4nkkkm2 “A split of a shared file lands without blocking other work” have all their tasks done and wait only for done. What is left is TK-dtybnlcg “bl_ci.py holds the CI readers and the red-pipeline command”, TK-urxtzpya “bl_view.py holds horizon and the read-only views” and then TK-xs5zfyo5 “backlog.py is the facade: its commands, usage and dispatch only”, whose test fails when backlog.py defines more than its dispatch. Second because it is short and the two bug sprints after it edit backlog.py: once it lands each fix goes into the module that owns its code, and the facade test keeps new code out of backlog.py. Each move is a shared-file move (kb-sprint run step 2): it starts when no claimed item holds backlog.py.
